site.description: Free PDF tools that run entirely in your browser: merge, split, compress, rotate, convert and protect PDFs. Your files never leave your device. No sign-up, no watermark.
site.homeTitle: Free PDF Tools That Never Upload Your Files

site.whySwitch: Why people switch to Scissor PDF

merge-pdf.name: Merge PDF
merge-pdf.short: Combine several PDFs into one file, in the order you choose.
merge-pdf.title: Merge PDF Files Free, Without Uploading
merge-pdf.description: Combine PDF files into one document in your browser. Drag to reorder, then merge. Files are never uploaded. Free, no sign-up, no watermark.
merge-pdf.lead: Combine several PDFs into one document, in the order you want. Everything happens on your device, so even confidential files stay private.
steps: Choose or drop the PDF files you want to combine. You can add more at any time.
Drag the files into the order they should appear in the final document.
Select Merge PDFs, then download the combined file.

sections.h: What is kept when you merge
sections.p: Every page keeps its original size, orientation, text, images, links and fillable form fields. Bookmarks from the first document are kept. The merged file is a standard PDF that opens in any reader, including Preview, Adobe Acrobat and every web browser.

There is no limit on the number of files or pages. Very large documents are limited only by your device's memory. A modern laptop handles several hundred megabytes comfortably. If a merged file turns out bigger than you need, run it through Compress PDF afterwards.

faqs.q: Are my files uploaded when I merge PDFs?
faqs.a: No. Scissor PDF runs a PDF engine written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly inside your browser tab. Your files are read from your disk into the page's memory, processed there and saved back to your device. The site has no upload endpoint, and its Content Security Policy blocks the page from sending data to any other server.

faqs.q: How do I change the order of the files?
faqs.a: Drag any file card to a new position before you merge. The final document follows the order of the cards from left to right, top to bottom.

faqs.q: Can I merge only some pages of a PDF?
faqs.a: Merge combines whole documents. To use only some pages, open the file in Extract pages first, then merge the result. Or merge everything and remove pages with Delete pages.

faqs.q: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?
faqs.a: Remove the password with Unlock PDF first (you need to know it), then merge.

faqs.q: Is it free? Do I need an account?
faqs.a: It is free, with no account, no daily task limit and no watermark added to your documents. Because the work happens on your own computer, there is no server cost per file for us to recover.

split-pdf.name: Split PDF
split-pdf.short: Cut a PDF into several files by page ranges or every few pages.
split-pdf.title: Split PDF Free, Without Uploading
split-pdf.description: Split a PDF into separate files by page ranges, every N pages or one file per page. Runs in your browser, so files are never uploaded. Free, no sign-up.
split-pdf.lead: Cut one PDF into several smaller files: by custom page ranges, into equal parts, or one file per page. Your document never leaves your device.
steps: Choose or drop the PDF you want to split.
Pick how to split it: custom ranges such as 1-3, 4-10, a fixed number of pages per file, or every page on its own.
Select Split PDF. You get one PDF, or a ZIP archive when the split produces several files.

sections.p: Custom ranges give you full control: type 1-5, 6-12, 13 to get three files. Fixed size cuts the document into parts of the same length, which is handy for scanned batches. Every page produces one PDF per page.
Split divides the whole document into several files. To pull just a few pages out into one new file, Extract pages is quicker.

faqs.q: How do I write page ranges?
faqs.a: Separate ranges with commas. Use a hyphen for a range and a single number for one page, for example 1-3, 5, 8-12. Each range becomes its own PDF.

faqs.q: Why do I get a ZIP file?
faqs.a: When a split produces more than one PDF, they are packed into a single ZIP so you only download once. Every operating system opens ZIP files with a double-click.

compress-pdf.name: Compress PDF
compress-pdf.short: Make a PDF smaller for email and uploads, with quality you choose.
compress-pdf.title: Compress PDF Free, Without Uploading
compress-pdf.description: Reduce PDF file size in your browser. Choose lossless, recommended or strong compression. Files are never uploaded. Free, no sign-up, no watermark.
compress-pdf.lead: Shrink a PDF so it fits email limits and upload forms. Choose how hard to compress, and see exactly how much smaller the file became. Nothing is uploaded.
steps: Choose or drop the PDF you want to make smaller.
Pick a level: Lossless keeps every pixel, Recommended balances size and quality, Strong makes the smallest file.
Select Compress PDF, check the new size, and download.

sections.p: Every level removes unused objects, packs the file structure into compressed object streams and compresses any uncompressed data. Recommended and Strong also re-encode large photos as JPEG and scale down images larger than needed for screen and office printing: up to 2200 pixels on the long side for Recommended, 1400 for Strong. Text and vector graphics are never rasterised, so they stay sharp and searchable.

Scanned documents and PDFs full of photos usually shrink the most, often by 70 to 95 percent. PDFs that are mostly text are already compact and may shrink only a little. If the result is not smaller, the original was already well optimised.

faqs.q: Which compression level should I choose?
faqs.a: Start with Recommended. It typically cuts photo-heavy PDFs by more than half while staying sharp on screen and in print. Use Strong when you must get under a strict size limit, and Lossless when the images must not change at all.

faqs.q: Will the text in my PDF become blurry?
faqs.a: No. Only embedded photos are re-encoded. Text, fonts and vector drawings are kept exactly as they were.

faqs.q: How do I get a PDF under 1 MB or 2 MB for an upload form?
faqs.a: Try Strong compression. If it is still too big, split the document with Split PDF, or remove pages you do not need with Delete pages, then compress again.

Drag pages into a new order. Use the buttons on each page to rotate or delete it.
Select Save PDF to download the reorganised document.

jpg-to-pdf.short: Turn photos and scans (JPG, PNG, HEIC, WebP) into a PDF.
jpg-to-pdf.title: JPG to PDF: Convert Images Free, No Upload
jpg-to-pdf.description: Convert JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC images to one PDF in your browser. Reorder, choose page size and margins. Photos are never uploaded. Free, no sign-up.
jpg-to-pdf.lead: Turn photos, screenshots and scanned pages into a single PDF. JPEGs are embedded at their original quality, and nothing is uploaded.
steps: Choose or drop your images: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, or HEIC on Safari.

Fit makes each page the same shape as its image, which is best for photos and screenshots. A4 and Letter place each image centred on standard paper, turning the page to landscape for wide images, which is best for documents you will print.

protect-pdf.title: Password Protect PDF (AES-256), No Upload
protect-pdf.description: Encrypt a PDF with a password using AES-256, and optionally block printing or copying. Runs in your browser, the file and password never leave your device.
protect-pdf.lead: Encrypt a PDF so it can only be opened with your password. Encryption runs on your device, so neither the document nor the password is ever sent anywhere.

sections.h: Choose a password you will remember

Create your signature: draw it, type your name in a handwriting style, or upload a photo of it.

sections.h: Three ways to create a signature
sections.p: Draw it on screen, which works especially well with a finger or an Apple Pencil. Type your name and pick a handwriting style. Or upload a photo of your signature on white paper: the paper is made transparent so only the ink appears on the document.

sections.p: Scissor PDF adds a visual signature, the same as signing a printout and scanning it. It does not add a certificate-based digital signature. That is accepted for most everyday documents such as forms, rental agreements and permission slips; check the requirements when a document asks for a qualified or certified electronic signature.

how.title: How Scissor PDF Edits PDFs Without Uploading Them
how.description: Scissor PDF runs a Rust PDF engine compiled to WebAssembly inside your browser. Learn how local processing works and how to verify that no file is uploaded.
how.lead: Your browser downloads the PDF engine, not the other way round. Here is what happens when you use a tool, and how you can check it yourself.
how.body:
The short version

Scissor PDF never receives your files. When you open a tool, your browser downloads the website and a PDF engine. When you choose a file, it is read into the memory of your browser tab, processed by that engine on your own processor, and the result is handed back to you as a download. Closing the tab erases everything.

What runs where

The PDF engine that merges, splits, reorders, rotates, compresses, numbers, watermarks, encrypts and decrypts PDFs is written in Rust, using the open-source lopdf library, and compiled to WebAssembly. WebAssembly is a sandboxed format every modern browser runs at close to native speed. It runs in a background worker so the page stays responsive.

Page previews and PDF to JPG use PDF.js, the open-source renderer built into Firefox, also running locally.

The server is a plain static file host. It has no upload endpoint, no database and no application code, so there is nothing that could accept a document.

Verify it yourself

Open your browser's developer tools, switch to the Network tab and use any tool. You will see the page's own files load, and no request carrying your document. You can also disconnect from the internet after the page has loaded: every tool keeps working.

The site also sends a strict Content Security Policy that tells your browser to block the page from contacting any other server, so even a mistake in our code could not send your files elsewhere.

Works offline, installs like an app

After your first visit, a service worker stores the site and engine in your browser's cache, so the tools open and work with no connection. In Chrome or Edge, choose Install from the address bar. In Safari, choose Add to Dock (Mac) or Add to Home Screen (iPhone and iPad).

Limits of local processing

Because the work happens on your device, very large files are limited by its memory. Several hundred megabytes are fine on a typical laptop, and phones handle everyday documents. Speed depends on your processor rather than on a server queue, which in practice is usually faster than uploading and downloading.

privacy.lead: Short, because there is little to say: we never receive your documents.
privacy.body:
Your files

Files you open in Scissor PDF are processed entirely in your browser and are never transmitted to us or to anyone else. We cannot see, store, share or recover them.

Passwords

Passwords you type into Protect PDF or Unlock PDF are used only in your browser to encrypt or decrypt the file, and are never transmitted or stored.

What our server sees

Like any website, our server and content delivery network receive standard request information when your browser downloads the site's pages and files: IP address, requested address, time, and browser user agent. This is used only to operate and secure the service and to count aggregate traffic, and is not combined with other data or sold.

Cookies and tracking

Scissor PDF sets no cookies of its own and uses no advertising trackers. Your browser stores the site's files for offline use, and may keep a file briefly in local storage when you choose "Continue with" to pass a result to another tool; it is removed as soon as the next tool opens it.
